newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Telecom denies talk of merger with KDD.
newsitem.headline: Japan Telecom denies talk of merger with KDD.

text.p: The president of Japan Telecom Co on Wednesday denied market rumours that it may merge with Kokusai Denshin Denwa Co once KDD is permitted to operate domestic telecommunications services.

"A merger in general slows the growth of companies. It is unlikely that we will take such a measure at a time when Japan's communications market is so volatile," Koichi Sakata said, adding that alliances would make much more sense.
In mid-August, KDD's shares rose to a 1996 high of 12,500 yen, following the release of analysts' reports that mentioned the possibility of a merger between the two firms.
KDD closed at 11,300 yen on Wednesday, down 300 yen.
The Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications said late last year that domestic phone operators, except for Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp, could move into international communications services.
KDD, which is at present prohibited from offering domestic services, is expected to obtain approval for domestic services in the not too distant future.
